decisions.reason: As a multi-item dietary supplement range that fits the firm's stated consumer-health expansion, the sunk launch effort and visible commitment make management inclined to continue it.
This supplement had standalone promotion and supports the broadening of the portfolio, so management would tend to justify the earlier investment and keep it unless failure were unmistakable.

Although less prominently committed than A or B, it still extends the established supplement line and disappointing demand can still be framed as a niche or temporary issue rather than grounds for withdrawal.

Despite the earlier Valsartan-related problem, the firm has already borne regulatory and market-entry costs and can treat past setbacks as external and temporary, which favors staying with the product.

The OTC migraine product represents a visible step in portfolio expansion, and management would be reluctant to reverse a publicly launched new category after committing development and commercialization resources.
